result:
Fixed. All suites pass.

## The bug

`Semaphore::permits` is a single `AtomicUsize` packing two things: the permit count above `PERMIT_SHIFT`, and the `CLOSED` flag in bit 0. `forget_permits` was the one writer that rebuilt the whole word from the permit count alone (`tokio/src/sync/batch_semaphore.rs:376`):

```rust
let curr = curr_bits >> Self::PERMIT_SHIFT;   // drops the CLOSED bit
let new  = curr.saturating_sub(n);
self.permits.compare_exchange_weak(curr_bits, new << Self::PERMIT_SHIFT, ...)
//                                             ^ CLOSED written back as 0
```

The shift-right dropped the flag and the shift-left wrote a zero into its place, so any `forget_permits` call on a closed semaphore cleared `CLOSED`. Since `is_closed`, `try_acquire`, and `poll_acquire` all read closedness from that bit, the semaphore silently reverted to open and began issuing permits again — `close()` is documented as permanent.

## The fix

Carry the flag bit across the CAS:

```rust
// The `CLOSED` bit lives below `PERMIT_SHIFT`, so it must be carried
// over explicitly; forgetting permits must not reopen the semaphore.
let new_bits = (new << Self::PERMIT_SHIFT) | (curr_bits & Self::CLOSED);
```

Reading `curr_bits` (the CAS-compared value) rather than re-loading keeps this correct under concurrent `close()`: if a close lands between load and CAS, the exchange fails and the retry picks up the flag.

I checked the other four writers to that word for the same mistake — none share it. `close` (`fetch_or`) and `add_permits_locked` (`fetch_add` of an already-shifted value) are bit-safe by construction, and `try_acquire:287` / `poll_acquire:443` only reach their CAS after returning early on `CLOSED`, so the bit is zero in both the expected and new values.

## Verification

`forget_closed` from the test commit fails on the unmodified tree (`git stash`-verified) and passes with the fix; the other 17 tests in that file pass either way. Full run: `sync_semaphore`, `sync_semaphore_owned`, `sync_mutex`, `sync_rwlock`, `sync_mpsc`, `sync_oneshot`, `sync_broadcast`, plus the 137 `--lib` unit tests (which include `sync/tests/semaphore_batch.rs`) — all green.

Two caveats on what I did *not* run: `rustfmt` and `clippy` aren't installed in this environment, so the new lines are hand-matched to surrounding style rather than tool-verified (I did confirm they're under 100 columns). The loom models in `sync/tests/loom_semaphore_batch.rs` also weren't run — they need a separate `--cfg loom` build. Neither seems likely to be affected, but you may want both in CI.
